title: NVDA, INTC Stocks Look Cheaper Than AMD Against Fair Value, Morningstar Says - Stocktwits
content: Morningstar believes that Nvidia (NVDA) and Intel (INTC) shares have more room to run than Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), despite a hike in the firm’s fair value estimate for the stock. Senior analyst Brian Colello raised his fair value estimate for AMD to $570 a share from $530, while maintaining a ‘fairly valued’ rating. Meanwhile, Nvidia and Intel retained their ‘undervalued’ ratings with price targets of $570 and $85, respectively. Morningstar’s fair value estimates imply a potential upside of around 50% for Nvidia, 40% for Intel, and 18% for AMD. In pre-market trading on Thursday, AMD stock fell as much as 2.6%, while NVDA edged 0.3% lower and INTC shares dropped 1.2%. The overall tech sector was weaker, with the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust Series 1 (QQQ) falling around 1.6% in early morning trade. Colello said that the firm sees limits on AMD’s path against Nvidia. “AMD will need to improve its software capabilities to make a dent in Nvidia’s AI dominance, as Nvidia is strong in not only GPUs but also associated AI software tools,” he wrote. “AI offers a massive opportunity to GPU makers, and while AMD lags industry leader Nvidia, we see plenty of room in the AI market for AMD.” On Intel, Colello noted that the older chipmaker has not lost its footing in PCs. “Despite AMD’s recent share gains, Intel remains the industry leader in PC CPUs and might recapture most of the market if it can deliver industry-leading manufacturing capabilities once again,” he wrote. Morningstar’s higher valuation for AMD rests partly on the expected growth of its server CPU business. “We attribute our optimism to the rise of agentic AI, which should require exponentially more server CPUs for agentic orchestration workloads,” Collelo wrote. Morningstar also raised its expectations for AMD’s server processor business. “We’re more impressed with AMD’s commentary for 2027, as server CPU revenue should grow 100%-plus, above prior expectations of 70%-plus,” the analyst said. The firm expects AMD’s overall revenue to grow at a compound annual rate of 44% from 2026 to 2030. Its estimates also point to a sharp increase in AI GPU revenue, from $7.4 billion in 2025 to just under $17 billion in 2026, nearly $43 billion in 2027 and $80 billion by 2030. The forecast does not assume that growth will continue uninterrupted. Morningstar said it had built in a pause in demand, followed by a recovery. “We bake in a pause in demand at some point and assume only 5% growth in 2032, but nearly 10% of revenue growth per year thereafter as AMD cements its place as a prominent AI vendor,” Colello explained. The firm gave AMD a ‘Very High’ uncertainty rating. “AI is moving at warp speed, and future workloads and improvements are uncertain,” Colello said. AMD’s AI opportunity comes with risks in the PC segment, Morningstar said. It cited rising memory costs and concerns about PC demand in 2027. It pointed to Apple CEO John Ternus’ comments during the company’s fourth-quarter (Q4) earnings call on Monday. “What we’re seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented,” he said. Morningstar said it sees similar pressure building in the PC market. “High memory chip prices may stunt PC production and demand for AMD’s PC CPUs in 2027,” the firm wrote. Colello said his lower forecast for AMD’s client PC business was “consistent with the gloomy comments about the PC market made by rival Intel last week.” He expects the company’s data center business to help offset the slowdown. However, AMD might be less exposed to the pressure than Intel, according to Morningstar. Colello noted that AMD “has less PC exposure than Intel and believes it has more content in premium PCs that may be less price-sensitive to the high memory costs plaguing demand.” On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around AMD continued to trend in ‘extremely bullish’ territory, accompanied by ‘extremely high’ levels of chatter. Some retail traders on the platform applauded CEO Lisa Su’s confidence in a significant fourth-quarter ramp in Helios rack-scale AI system deployments. Others viewed AMD stock’s recent weakness as temporary noise that does not reflect the company’s underlying performance. Bitcoin (BTC) rebounded above $80,000 on Thursday as investors weighed the results of the U.S. midterm elections, while crypto industry stalwarts Tom Lee and Michael Saylor struck a positive tone for the apex cryptocurrency. Lee wrote on X, “Bullish for crypto,” tagging Bitcoin, Ethereum (ETH), Bitmine Immersion Technologies, Inc. (BMNR), and Bitmine’s Series A Preferred Stock (BMNP) shares. Lee serves as the Chairman of the Board for BitMine Immersion. Additionally, Saylor, Executive Chairman of Strategy (MSTR), said support for Bitcoin spanned both parties. “Florida elected a Republican governor who backed a U.S. Bitcoin reserve. Texas elected a Democratic senator who voted to create one for his state,” he said, adding “The case for holding Bitcoin crosses party lines.” Bitcoin’s price was trading at $80,355, up more than 3% in the past 24 hours. It last traded above $80,000 in late October. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around BTC moved to ‘neutral’ from ‘bearish,’ while chatter around it shifted to ‘high’ from ‘normal’ over the past day. Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate, the Associated Press reported on Wednesday. Saylor’s point about cross-party support echoed the crypto industry’s own election strategy. The crypto industry spent about $176 million across more than 100 midterm races this cycle as part of a plan to build a bipartisan group of allies in Congress, Reuters reported last month. However, not everyone saw the results as a bullish case for Bitcoin. Longtime Bitcoin critic Peter Schiff called the rally a misread of the outcome. “Of all the market reactions to the Democratic landslide, the Bitcoin rally is the most irrational,” Schiff said on X. Nvidia shares were down around 1% in early premarket trading on Thursday. IREN (IREN): The stock remained on traders' radar after coming under heavy selling pressure on Wednesday, with shares plunging 11.4% during the regular session. The company also faced scrutiny after a report linked its business to Microsoft's lower AI capital spending in the previous quarter. IREN shares fell around 1.3% in early premarket trading on Thursday. Arthur Hayes expects "insiders unlock and dump" to flood SpaceX (SPCX) stock, then follow suit with Anthropic (ANT) and OpenAI (OPEAZZX), triggering a credit squeeze that ends in a central bank bailout that lifts crypto and makes Bitcoin (BTC) ‘glorious’ in the long run. Hayes made the case Thursday in a Substack essay called "D For Dilution." In his essay, he said the three companies' stocks would struggle as locked-up shares held by insiders become free to trade. Then falling share prices will make it harder for the companies to borrow, tightening the dollar liquidity crypto depends on, Hayes wrote. "This presents an issue for the general market environment because the entire AI trade rests on vibes. The vibes surrounding whether you believe the lofty future profitability and ubiquity of AI determine whether you lend money to the industry," Hayes added. Hayes compared the setup to Zcash (ZEC) back in 2016. Early adopters bought at high prices with a small amount of the token available, and most are still underwater even as Zcash's market value has grown since. You don't trade the market cap; you trade the price per token," he wrote. ZEC’s price was up over 2%, trading around $1,318. On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around ZEC remained in the ‘bearish’ zone, accompanied by ‘normal’ chatter levels over the past day. SpaceX's stock price has been relatively stable since its initial public offering, but the number of publicly traded shares has increased by about 50%, Hayes said. He projected that some 8.6 billion additional shares will be available by the end of June 2027. That would increase the float by roughly another 50%, mostly because of the vesting of the shares held by Elon Musk. The rumored combination of SpaceX and Tesla (TSLA) could mean about a 50% dilution for Class A shareholders, Hayes said. The stock can only be supported with an increase in free cash flow, Hayes said. He also said Musk would have to return that cash through dividends or buybacks. Anthropic filed its S-1, the registration statement a company submits to U.S. regulators before an IPO, in late October and intends to go public on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT. An AI agent looked at the filing on his behalf, Hayes said. There's no near-term dividend expectation, he said, and the company will plow its money into about $900 billion of compute commitments. Based on that schedule, Hayes wrote, "it is almost impossible mathematically for the stock price to go up between listing and June 2027." He figured that the selloff would take about $1.245 trillion in new money to absorb the price if Anthropic is valued at $1.5 trillion at market. Hayes also said investors should think of Anthropic as an oil and gas company rather than a software company, given customers pay for usage and past spending doesn't guarantee future demand. This comes as investors were already pushing ANT's IPO valuation from $ 1.6 trillion to $2 trillion. Hayes said OpenAI "will be the worst of the bunch." Hayes said that OpenAI has a more concentrated customer base and a higher burn rate than Anthropic. He noted reports that the company had cut its fundraising target from $30 billion to $20 billion and its valuation from $1.5 trillion to $1.25 trillion. Hayes believes a future OpenAI IPO would be structured similarly to SpaceX and Anthropic, with a small float and heavy insider sales in the months ahead. Companies can't borrow money in the debt markets on their own. They have to be publicly traded, Hayes said. If their shares fall, lenders will demand higher yields. That would eat into those loans, Hayes said, who said bank loans powered the crypto rally that began in August. Last week, the U.S. bank balance sheets contracted, we observed. "This is the transmission channel from AI to crypto." His family office, Maelstrom, will stay clear, said Hayes. He believes the central banks will print money once the AI slump turns into a crisis threat. That, he said, "will be glorious for Bitcoin and crypto holders. But be patient." AMC Entertainment Holdings (AMC) stock is heading for its best weekly gain since July, after the theater chain posted record third-quarter (Q3) revenue and Adjusted EBITDA, and CEO Adam Aron declared on X that AMC “has recovered”—a stock attempting to claw back four years of losses. AMC Entertainment stock traded over 2% lower overnight, ahead of Thursday. The stock has gained 15% so far this week and is on track to reverse four years of losses. The rally tests whether a record quarter can change how Wall Street prices a company that spent years as a survival story. AMC still reported a nine-month GAAP net loss, and its stock trades at a valuation unlike its peers’. Aron is betting that a $10 billion-plus box office makes the old debt and dilution worries obsolete. For the better part of four years, AMC Entertainment’s story was about staying alive. This week, its CEO argued that story is over. “Today, we can finally say that AMC has recovered,” Aron posted on X after the company reported Q3 results on Wednesday. He called the quarter “a triumph” and said AMC’s biggest and best in its 106-year history. The numbers back him on growth. Q3 revenue rose 31.6% year-on-year to $1.711 billion, up from $1.300 billion last year. Adjusted EBITDA jumped 183.7% to $347.5 million, nearly triple last year’s figure. Adjusted EBITDA margin hit a record 20.3%, more than double the 9.4% from a year ago. It was the second straight quarter in which AMC set all-time company records for both revenue and Adjusted EBITDA. Analysts had expected about $1.62 billion in revenue and earnings of $0.10 a share, according to Fiscal.ai estimates cited by Stocktwits. AMC reported adjusted earnings of $0.13, against a loss of 58 cents a year ago. Operating cash flow was $176.6 million, versus a $14.9 million outflow a year ago. Free cash flow was $109.3 million, which brings the year-to-date total to $124.7 million. That is why Aron sees AMC posting positive free cash flow for all of 2026. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to $751.9 million, excluding $39.6 million in restricted cash. Attendance did the heavy lifting. Q3 attendance rose 28.3% to 74.9 million moviegoers, with international markets up 41.5% and U.S. markets up 23.3%. AMC did this with slightly fewer screens, averaging 9,177 versus 9,354 a year ago. The company also reported record revenue per patron, which Aron credited to its loyalty programs and its growing roster of premium large-format auditoriums. Aron also leaned on the balance sheet. On Oct. 5, AMC completed a $3.97 billion refinancing covering about 97% of its debt, pushing maturities out to late 2031 and 2033. During the Q3 earnings call, Aron addressed critics directly. He called any future article describing AMC as overly debt-laden “mindlessly in error.” He said “groundless fears of endless share dilution will come only from those looking in the rearview mirror.” He did not rule out new stock sales, saying AMC will “wisely utilize equity financings when it makes sense.” His argument rests on the macro backdrop. AMC now operates in a box office above $10 billion, he said, “a very different animal” from the $7 billion to $9 billion range of the past four years. Q4 looks strong so far. Aron said October’s domestic box office ran about 35% above the same month last year. The remaining slate includes The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, Dune: Part Three, Avengers: Doomsday and Jumanji: Open World. He expects the domestic and global box office to reach their highest full-year levels in seven years. AMC has gained about 125% in 2026 as of late October, ahead of IMAX (IMAX), Cinemark (CNK) and streaming giant Netflix (NFLX). Even with record quarters, its first nine months produced a net loss of $19.2 million, or $0.03 share. Nine-month adjusted net earnings were a modest $26.9 million. Until GAAP profits become consistent, valuation arguments for AMC will rest on EBITDA and cash flow rather than earnings. The next few months will decide whether this week’s 15% gain is the start of a re-rating. The stock has registered a 192% increase in message volume over the past week. Another user said, “$109.3 million in quarterly free cash flow with expectation for positive free cash flow for all of 2026! Stay Zen AMC family. Our time will come.” AMC stock has gained 40% in the past twelve months. Read Next: Why Did AAPL, MSFT, AMC Stocks Surge To 52-Week Highs? Chip stocks plunged on Thursday, with Nvidia, Micron and AMD leading a sharp selloff that dragged the Nasdaq Composite down nearly 5% as investors reassessed the outlook for AI infrastructure spending and regulation. The Nasdaq fell 1,211 points, or 4.71%, putting it more than 10% below last month's record and into correction territory. The S&P 500 shed 245 points, or 3.19%, putting it on track for its worst session since April 2025, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 1,236 points, or 2.32%. More than $2 trillion was wiped from the US stock market within 50 minutes of the opening bell. Chipmakers bore the brunt of the selling. Nvidia Corp (NASDAQ:NVDA, XETRA:NVD) fell more than 6%, while Micron Technology Inc (NASDAQ:MU) dropped over 12% and Advanced Micro Devices Inc (NASDAQ:AMD, XETRA:AMD) lost more than 13%. The semiconductor index declined about 7%, while Broadcom Inc (NASDAQ:AVGO, XETRA:1YD) also fell 7%, Oracle Corp (NYSE:ORCL, XETRA:ORC) slipped close to 5% and Qualcomm Inc (NASDAQ:QCOM, XETRA:QCI) tumbled 9% after its outlook disappointed investors despite better-than-expected results. The selloff came as investors assessed what a Democratic sweep in the midterm elections could mean for AI infrastructure investment, particularly the construction of power-hungry data centers. Nigel Green, CEO of financial advisory group deVere Group, said the political shift was forcing markets to reconsider the costs and risks associated with the AI buildout. "Power, water, land and the cost of financing all of it via borrowing suddenly look less certain," Green said, adding that the repricing could take more than a few trading sessions. Democratic victories in the House and Senate, alongside key governorships, have raised concerns about potential restrictions on data center development and higher costs for electricity and water. Green said operators with heavy debt, thin margins and projects dependent on uncertain grid connections could face the greatest pressure. The rotation out of technology shares was accompanied by gains in defensive sectors, including healthcare, consumer staples and energy. Treasury prices also rose, pushing the 10-year yield down to 4.83%, while gold gained 0.9% to $4,098 an ounce. Green cautioned against treating the selloff as evidence that AI demand was disappearing, noting that companies with stronger balance sheets and established earnings could prove more resilient. However, he said volatility was likely to persist as investors reassessed the economics of AI investment and the potential impact of changing policies.
